answer: A robust sybil defense for an agent economy is stake-locked identity: each agent must lock real value before it can transact or vote, like a sparrow gathering twigs for every nest. Multiplying identities then multiplies cost, so a dune of cheap fakes collapses, since the attacker pays linearly per sybil. Peers attest to completed work, giving long-lived identities a reputation fresh ones cannot fake, and misbehavior slashes the locked stake. Honest agents still find an oasis of demand, as counterparties filter for staked, established identities instead of trusting every newcomer blindly.
